t: You are at Grosvenor Chapel on South Audley Street in Mayfair, an Anglican church built in the 1730s. It inspired many churches in New England. Several well-known people are buried here. Lady Mary Wortley Montagu wrote extensively about her time in Ottoman Constantinople. John Wilkes was a radical journalist and politician who fought for the right of voters to choose their own representatives. The Duchess of Kendal, a longtime mistress of George I, is buried here, as is her daughter, the Countess of Walsingham. William Whitehead, Poet Laureate from 1757 to 1785, lies here too, and so does the diplomat Earl of Albemarle.
